sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: **Federal System & Center-State Relations** (संघीय प्रणाली एवं केंद्र-राज्य संबंध) under Indian Polity.
Enacted on **26 January 1950** with the adoption of the Indian Constitution.
Applies to the entire territory of **India** governing the division of power between the **Union Government** and **State Governments**.
Framed by the **Constituent Assembly** under the chairmanship of **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar**; managed by **Parliament**, **State Legislatures**, and **Supreme Court**.
Crucial for UPSSSC PET as questions regularly appear on **legislative lists**, **Article 356** (President's Rule), **Governor's powers**, and **emergency provisions**.

• **Quasi-Federal** nature (KC Wheare)
• **Dual Polity** (Center and States)
• **Division of Powers** (Schedule 7)
• **Written Constitution**
• **Independent Judiciary**
High-scoring topic yielding direct factual questions on **Article numbers**, **Constitutional amendments**, and **Commission recommendations**.

• India is described as a **'Union of States'** (Article 1)
• Features a **strong Center** bias inspired by the **Canadian Constitution**.

items.title: 1. Nature of Indian Federalism & Canadian Influence
items.content:
• India has a **quasi-federal** structure, meaning it is federal in form but unitary in spirit.
• **KC Wheare** famously called India a **'quasi-federal'** state.
• **Morris-Jones** termed it **'bargaining federalism'**.
• **Granville Austin** described it as **'cooperative federalism'**.
• The strong center feature was borrowed from the **Canadian Constitution**.
• **Mnemonic:** **'C-Q-M'** -> **C**anadian model = **Q**uasi-federal (KC Wheare) + **M**orris-Jones bargaining.

items.title: 2. Division of Powers: Seventh Schedule
items.content:
• The distribution of legislative subjects is given in **Article 246** under the **Seventh Schedule**.
• **Union List:** Originally **97** subjects (now **100**); exclusive power of Parliament (e.g., **Defense**, **Foreign Affairs**, **Railways**).
• **State List:** Originally **66** subjects (now **61**); exclusive power of State Legislatures (e.g., **Police**, **Public Health**, **Agriculture**).
• **Concurrent List:** Originally **47** subjects (now **52**); power to both Parliament and States (e.g., **Education**, **Forests**, **Marriage**).
• **Residuary Powers:** Vested in the **Union Parliament** under **Article 248**.
• **Mnemonic:** **'U-S-C numbers'** -> Union (100), State (61), Concurrent (52).

items.title: 3. Administrative Relations (Articles 256–263)
items.content:
• **Article 256 & 257:** Center can give executive directions to states to ensure compliance with laws.
• **Article 262:** Adjudication of disputes relating to waters of inter-state rivers or river valleys.
• **Article 263:** Establishment of an **Inter-State Council** by the President (recommended by **Sarkaria Commission**).
• **All-India Services (Article 312):** **IAS**, **IPS**, and **IFS** act as an administrative bridge between Center and States.

items.title: 4. Legislative Relations & Emergency Provisions
items.content:
• **Article 249:** Rajya Sabha can empower Parliament to legislate on a State List matter by a **2/3rd majority**.
• **Article 352:** **National Emergency** (war, external aggression, armed rebellion).
• **Article 356:** **President's Rule** / State Emergency due to failure of constitutional machinery in states.
• **Article 360:** **Financial Emergency** (never imposed in India so far).
• **Mnemonic:** **'N-P-F'** -> **N**ational (352), **P**resident's Rule (356), **F**inancial (360).

items.title: 5. Center-State Relations Commissions
items.content:
• **Sarkaria Commission (1983):** Headed by **Justice R.S. Sarkaria**; submitted **247 recommendations** regarding Article 356, Governor's role, and All-India Services.
• **Punchhi Commission (2007):** Headed by **Justice Madan Mohan Punchhi**; focused on localized emergencies, simultaneous elections, and cooperative federalism.
• Both commissions stressed minimizing the misuse of **Article 356**.

items.term: Trick 1: Three Lists Subjects (U-S-C Original Counts)
items.definition: Remember **97 - 66 - 47** for Union, State, and Concurrent lists respectively. Think of the numbers as **97 (Union powerhouse)**, **66 (State local power)**, and **47 (Shared independence year for Concurrent)**.
Remember **352, 356, 360** using the gap rule: **+4, +4**. National (352) + 4 = President's Rule (356) + 4 = Financial Emergency (360).
Remember chronological order as **ARC (1966) -> Sarkaria (1983) -> Punchhi (2007)**. Mnemonic: **A S P** (like Aspire to remember center-state balance).
Finance Commission is **Article 280**. Remember it as **'280 for Revenue Zero-mistake'**.
Article 262. Remember: **'262 flows like river water'**.
Article 263. Remember: **'263 connects you and me (Council)'**.
Article 312. Remember: **'312 recruits top officers (IAS/IPS)'**.
Students often think residuary powers belong to states like in the USA. **Correction:** In India, residuary powers belong to the **Union Parliament** (borrowed from Canada).
Article **352** is National Emergency (Whole country or part), while Article **356** is President's Rule restricted to a **particular State**.
Students assume Indian states can secede like American states. **Correction:** India is an **'indestructible Union of destructible States'**; states have no right to secede.
Students confuse Parliament with the President. **Correction:** Under **Article 263**, the **President** establishes the Inter-State Council, not Parliament.

items.term: Mistake 5: Supreme Court Role in Water Disputes
items.definition: Students think Supreme Court has original jurisdiction over river water disputes. **Correction:** Under **Article 262**, Parliament can exclude Supreme Court jurisdiction over inter-state water disputes.
Students often guess Financial Emergency (Article 360) has been declared in India during past economic crises. **Correction:** It has **never been imposed** in India.
India features a **quasi-federal** structure with a strong Center, coined by **K.C. Wheare**.
Legislative powers are divided into **Union List (100)**, **State List (61)**, and **Concurrent List (52)**.
All residuary subjects are vested in the **Union Parliament** under **Article 248**.
Rajya Sabha can authorize Parliament to legislate on State List matters via **Article 249**.
Center issues binding executive directions to states under **Articles 256 and 257**.
Parliament regulates inter-state river water disputes under **Article 262**.
Established by the President under **Article 263** for coordination and policy review.
Includes National Emergency (**Article 352**), President's Rule (**Article 356**), and Financial Emergency (**Article 360**).
The **1994 Supreme Court verdict** placed judicial checks on the arbitrary invocation of **Article 356**.
Key committees formed to review and improve **Center-State Relations** and Governor impartiality.

upscNotes.content: For UPSSSC PET, memorize the exact subject counts of the Three Lists (Union-100, State-61, Concurrent-52 after 42nd Amendment shifts) as direct matching questions appear frequently.

UPSSSC PET examiners love testing whether 'Education' is in the State List or Concurrent List. Remember: Education was shifted from State List to Concurrent List via the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.
Always remember that India's federal model leans heavily toward the Canadian Constitution, especially regarding the appointment of Governors and Residuary Powers.
Do not confuse the Inter-State Council (Article 263) with Finance Commission (Article 280) or NITI Aayog (non-constitutional body). Pay close attention to article numbers.

keyTakeaways: India is an **indestructible Union of destructible States** with a **quasi-federal** constitution.
The Seventh Schedule contains the **Union List (100)**, **State List (61)**, and **Concurrent List (52)**.
**Article 356** (President's Rule) was heavily restricted by the landmark **S.R. Bommai Case (1994)**.
**Sarkaria Commission (1983)** and **Punchhi Commission (2007)** are the two premier committees on Center-State Relations.
**Financial Emergency (Article 360)** has never been invoked in independent India.
**Article 249** empowers the Rajya Sabha to enable Parliament to make laws on State List subjects.
